rule: No blanket policies. All 23 application tables remain RLS-enabled with zero policies because browser roles receive no direct table privileges after the targeted Stage 5 revoke. Business access is intentionally mediated through issuer-gated Better Auth RPCs, validated participant portal token RPCs, public read/event RPCs, or service_role-only backend paths. Platform auth/storage tables remain out of scope.

approved browser roles and direct table CRUD operations

effective anon/authenticated/service_role GRANT review including MAINTAIN
positive owner/role/token tests through the supported RPC/Edge boundary

public banner and participant portal flows preserved through narrow RPCs
safe search_path and non-recursive helper review for authorization predicates

stage5-no-policy-table-acl-draft.sql: browser revoke and trusted service_role/postgres preservation

checks: All 23 application-owned tables exist, remain owned by postgres, retain RLS, and have zero policies.
anon and authenticated have no effective SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, REFERENCES, TRIGGER, or MAINTAIN privilege on the 23 tables.
No explicit PUBLIC ACL remains on the 23 application tables.
service_role retains CRUD on the 20 designated public backend tables and has no direct table grants on the three private tables.
The assertion ran after the Stage 5 no-policy ACL draft and the Stage 7 portal parent-session hardening on the disposable restore.
limitations: This acceptance covers direct table RLS/ACL boundaries on the disposable schema restore only.
It does not complete the separate SECURITY DEFINER caller/issuer/token audit, which remains a Production cutover blocker.
It does not apply any grants, policies, DDL, or DML to Production.

notes: The five chat_group tables retain RLS enabled, zero policies, and no direct browser table privileges.

The retirement migration revokes PUBLIC/anon/authenticated table privileges, revokes EXECUTE on public/private chat RPCs, removes chat-named Realtime tables, and retains table rows for controlled archival.
The only remaining non-chat caller is admin_force_delete_competition on chat_groups; its legacy-issuer denial and Better Auth admin path are tested separately.
